h: Market town roots, East London energy
p: Romford has been a market town for centuries, with its market charter dating back to the 1200s, and it still has that busy, bustling feel. A trampoline session fits right in with that energy. If you're juggling a few ages, it helps to have a plan for whoever finishes first: older kids usually want every last second on the court, while little ones can flag after half an hour. Bring a snack for the car, because the post-bounce hunger arrives before you've even found your keys.

Getting here is easy, too. Romford station is on the Elizabeth line, so it's a straightforward ride from central London and the east, and plenty of buses run into the town centre. The Brewery shopping area, built on the site of the old Romford Brewery, has chain restaurants and a cinema if you fancy carrying on indoors.

For fresh air, Havering has some great green spaces a short drive out. Bedfords Park sits on a hillside with views over towards London and has a deer enclosure, which always goes down well with younger visitors. Havering Country Park is known for its grand avenue of giant redwood trees, a lovely, slightly unexpected sight on the edge of the capital. Bird lovers can head down to the RSPB reserve at Rainham Marshes, where boardwalks wind across the old marshland by the Thames. It's a nice contrast to an hour of bouncing, and it gives everyone a chance to cool down properly.
